model.title: Combating Foreign Threats to Main Street Act of 2026
model.meta: Small Business Committee · Rep. Roger Williams (R-TX)

summary.text: The bill would direct the Small Business Administration, working with federal agency heads, to create and share educational materials that help small businesses understand and guard against foreign adversary conduct that could materially harm them. The materials would cover how such conduct harms businesses, best practices for protecting intellectual property, sensitive information and supply chains, cybersecurity and data protection guidance, and the risks of foreign investment, joint ventures, and licensing deals with entities tied to foreign adversaries. They would also describe federal resources available to businesses and advise on protecting interests in foreign markets without unnecessarily restricting lawful trade. Starting October 1, 2027, the materials would be reviewed and updated each year, and the agency would have to notify two congressional small business committees if it determines an activity poses a significant risk to national or economic security.
